facts: Casual leave: every faculty member is entitled to 12 days of casual leave per calendar year, with no more than 4 consecutive days at a time.
Earned leave: 30 days per calendar year, which may be accumulated up to 240 days.
Teaching load: an Assistant Professor teaches 16 contact hours per week, an Associate Professor 14 hours and a Professor 12 hours.
Invigilation remuneration is Rs. 500 per session.
Evaluation remuneration is Rs. 40 per answer script.
Internal assessment marks must be uploaded to the examination portal within 7 working days after the end of the end-semester examinations.
A research seed grant of up to Rs. 2,00,000 per project may be sanctioned by the Research Committee.
Question paper setters are appointed by the Controller of Examinations from the approved panel. Each course requires 3 sets of question papers.
Setters must submit the question papers at least 21 days before the start of the end-semester examinations.
A moderation panel of 3 faculty members reviews every question paper for syllabus coverage and difficulty.
Question papers are placed in sealed envelopes with tamper-evident stickers.
The strong room has a dual lock that requires both the Controller of Examinations and the Registrar to open.
Papers are printed in the secure press room within 48 hours of the examination.
Any suspected leakage must be reported to the Controller of Examinations within 2 hours.
A setter responsible for a leak is debarred from paper setting for 3 years.
Moderation is considered when the class average ESE score in a course is below 45% of the maximum marks.
Moderation may add up to 5 marks to the ESE scores of the whole class, subject to the approval of the Moderation Committee.
Grace marks of up to 2 marks may be given to a student only to convert a fail into a pass, and only in 1 course per semester.
Moderation sheets are confidential and must not be shared with students.
Faculty members must not discuss moderation decisions or grace marks with students.
Moderation records are retained for 5 years in the office of the Controller of Examinations.
The Disciplinary Committee heard 9 cases between January and June 2025: 4 plagiarism, 3 examination malpractice and 2 hostel violations.
Case DC-2025-03: Student S-1042 (pseudonym), plagiarism in a mini project. Penalty: zero marks in the assignment and a written warning.
Case DC-2025-07: Student S-2210 (pseudonym), mobile phone found in the examination hall. Penalty: answer paper of the course cancelled.
Case DC-2025-11: Student S-3377 (pseudonym), hostel violation involving a prohibited cooking appliance. Penalty: fine of Rs. 2,000 and 2 weeks suspension from the hostel.
Case DC-2025-14: Student S-1042 (pseudonym), second plagiarism offence. Penalty: failure in the course.
The Committee chairperson for 2025 is Dr. R. Menon (fictional name).
The discretionary fee waiver pool for the academic year 2025-26 is Rs. 25,00,000.
The Principal may approve a waiver of up to Rs. 50,000 per student without reference to a committee. Larger waivers need the approval of the Governing Council.
This pool is not advertised publicly and the list of recipients is confidential.
Waivers from this pool are granted only after the Scholarship Committee has confirmed that the student does not qualify for any published scholarship.
Monthly salary bands: Assistant Professor Rs. 60,000 to Rs. 1,50,000; Associate Professor Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 1,90,000; Professor Rs. 1,40,000 to Rs. 2,40,000.
The approved annual operating budget for 2025-26 is Rs. 48 crore, of which 55% is allocated to salaries.
Salary bands are reviewed by the Governing Council every 3 years.
